section: Earthquakes - causes, seismic waves, measurement, distribution, effects
subsections: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: The Uttarkashi earthquake of 1991, with an approximate magnitude of 6.8, occurred in which setting?
accepted.x: The 1991 Uttarkashi earthquake occurred in the Himalayan thrust zone and had an approximate magnitude of 6.8.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the earthquake with its tectonic setting.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: The 1993 Latur earthquake was significant because it occurred in an intraplate region that had earlier been rated as which risk zone?
accepted.x: The Latur earthquake occurred in an intraplate region that was then classified as low-risk Zone I.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical-zone clue to distinguish a low-risk intraplate event.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Bhuj earthquake occurred on 26 January 2001 and had a magnitude of 7.7. The other pairs contain incorrect years or magnitudes.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year–magnitude pair and eliminate swapped entries.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: The Bhuj earthquake of 2001 led directly to which of the following institutional and legislative developments?
o: The enactment of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and the establishment of the NDMA
The creation of the Tsunami Early Warning System and GSI
The establishment of the National Centre for Seismology and the RISEQ app
The introduction of Zone VI under IS 1893: 2016
accepted.x: The 2001 Bhuj earthquake contributed to the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and the establishment of the National Disaster Management Authority.
accepted.tq: Link a major disaster to the institutional response that followed it.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gorkha earthquake:
1. It occurred in Nepal in 2015.
2. It had a magnitude of 7.8.
3. It occurred along the Main Himalayan Thrust.
4. It caused liquefaction in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 2015 Gorkha earthquake in Nepal had a magnitude of 7.8, occurred along the Main Himalayan Thrust and caused liquefaction in parts of the Gangetic plain.
accepted.tq: Verify the event through its year, magnitude, tectonic setting and secondary effect.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: The 2011 Tohoku earthquake in Japan was associated with which combination?
o: Pacific plate subduction, tsunami and Fukushima
Intraplate movement and the Disaster Management Act, 2005
Himalayan thrust zone and liquefaction in Bihar
accepted.x: The 2011 Tohoku earthquake had a magnitude of 9.0, occurred in the Pacific plate subduction setting and was associated with a tsunami and the Fukushima disaster.
accepted.tq: Match the earthquake with its distinctive tectonic setting and consequences.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: The February 2023 earthquake in the Turkey–Syria region occurred along which fault system?
accepted.x: The February 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake, of magnitude 7.8, occurred along the East Anatolian Fault between the Anatolian and Arabian plates.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named regional fault systems.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2025 Myanmar earthquake near Mandalay?
o: Magnitude 9.0; Pacific subduction zone; tsunami in Japan
Magnitude 6.2; Himalayan thrust zone; liquefaction in Bihar
Magnitude 7.8; East Anatolian Fault; movement of the Anatolian and Arabian plates
Magnitude 7.7; Sagaing Fault; strike-slip movement involving the Indian and Eurasian plates
accepted.x: The 2025 Mandalay earthquake had a magnitude of 7.7 and occurred along the Sagaing Fault, a strike-slip boundary involving the Indian and Eurasian plates. More than 2,000 people died.
accepted.tq: Use the fault type and plate pair to distinguish a recent earthquake event.
accepted.sec: Major earthquakes → place, year, setting

accepted.s: India forms part of which major seismic belt?
accepted.x: India lies in the Alpine-Himalayan seismic belt, which extends eastward through the North-East into Myanmar.
accepted.tq: Recall the major global seismic belt associated with India.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: The Indian Plate is moving approximately how far northward each year into the Eurasian Plate?
accepted.x: The Indian Plate moves northward into the Eurasian Plate at approximately 5 centimetres per year.
accepted.tq: Identify the central value in a set of plausible plate-motion rates.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which fault marks the Indian–Eurasian plate boundary in Myanmar?
accepted.x: In Myanmar, the Sagaing Fault marks the continuation of the Indian–Eurasian boundary through the eastern part of the seismic belt.
accepted.tq: Locate the named fault along the eastward continuation of the Himalayan seismic belt.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which of the following regions is NOT identified as a prone area for significant earthquake activity in India?
accepted.x: Kutch, the North-East and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are earthquake-prone areas. Visakhapatnam is cited as an example of a low-risk stable-shield area.
accepted.tq: Find the location that does not belong to the group of earthquake-prone regions.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Liquefaction is a particular concern in the Indo-Gangetic plain.
2. Peninsular faults associated with Latur and Koyna can produce earthquakes.
3. The Himalaya, North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands are among the earthquake-prone regions of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Earthquake vulnerability in India is associated with Himalayan and North-Eastern regions, liquefaction-prone alluvial plains, peninsular faults and the Andaman and Nicobar region.
accepted.tq: Combine regional distribution with the associated hazard or geological setting.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Under IS 1893:2016, which sequence correctly represents the seismic zones from lower to higher risk?
o: Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV, Zone V
Zone V, Zone IV, Zone III, Zone II
Zone III, Zone II, Zone V, Zone IV
Zone II, Zone IV, Zone III, Zone V
accepted.x: Under the four-zone map in force, Zone II represents low risk, Zone III moderate risk, Zone IV high risk and Zone V very high risk.
accepted.tq: Arrange the zones by increasing risk rather than by geographical location.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched under the seismic zoning classification in force?
accepted.x: Zone III is classified as a moderate-risk zone. Zone II is low, Zone IV is high and Zone V is very high risk.
accepted.tq: Check the exact risk label attached to each numerical zone.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which of the following areas is included in Zone V under the seismic zoning map in force?
accepted.x: Kutch is included in Zone V, the very-high-risk zone. Visakhapatnam and Hyderabad are examples of Zone II, while Vijayawada is cited under Zone III.
accepted.tq: Distinguish locations by their assigned seismic-risk zones.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Delhi, the remaining Himalayan foothills and the Indo-Gangetic belt are generally placed in which seismic zone?
accepted.x: Delhi, the rest of the Himalayan foothills and the Indo-Gangetic belt are cited as examples of Zone IV, the high-risk zone.
accepted.tq: Associate a regional cluster with its common seismic zone.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which of the following cities is cited as an example of a Zone III location?
accepted.x: Vijayawada is cited as an example of Zone III, which represents moderate risk. Visakhapatnam and Hyderabad are examples of Zone II.
accepted.tq: Separate nearby Andhra locations by their stated seismic classification.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Most of the state lies in Zones II and III.
2. Andhra Pradesh has no area in Zone V.
3. Andhra Pradesh is classified entirely as a very-high-risk state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Most of Andhra Pradesh lies in Zones II and III, and it has no area in Zone V. It is not entirely a very-high-risk state, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme statement while retaining the two precise regional facts.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which of the following States or Union Territories has no area in Zone V?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has no area in Zone V. Assam, Bihar and Jammu and Kashmir are identified as having areas in Zone V.
accepted.tq: Use the exception-based regional comparison to identify the outlier.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Zone I was merged into which zone after the 1993 Latur earthquake?
accepted.x: After the 1993 Latur earthquake, Zone I was merged into Zone II, resulting in the four-zone classification under IS 1893:2002.
accepted.tq: Link a classification change to the event that prompted it.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Withdrawal of IS 1893 (Part 1): 2025
B. Notification of IS 1893 (Part 1): 2025
C. 1993 Latur earthquake
D. Bhuj earthquake
accepted.x: The correct order is the 1993 Latur earthquake, the 2001 Bhuj earthquake, notification of the 2025 revision on 6 November 2025, and its withdrawal on 3 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the two intermediate dates.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: The revised IS 1893 (Part 1): 2025 was notified by BIS on which date?
accepted.x: BIS notified the revised IS 1893 (Part 1): 2025 on 6 November 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the notification date from the later withdrawal and review dates.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which feature was introduced by the IS 1893 (Part 1): 2025 revision?
o: The abolition of all seismic zones in India
The exclusion of the North-East from the highest-risk category
The restoration of Zone I as the lowest zone
A new top Zone VI covering parts of Kashmir, the North-East and Kutch
accepted.x: The 2025 revision introduced a new top Zone VI for parts of Kashmir, the North-East and Kutch, and placed more than 60% of India’s landmass in moderate-to-high zones.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive institutional change rather than a reversed zoning claim.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: The 2025 revision of IS 1893 was withdrawn on 3 March 2026 primarily after objections relating to which issue?
o: The inability to identify earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above
The absence of earthquake data from the North-East
The replacement of the National Seismological Network
The cost implications raised by MoHUA, Metro Rail corporations and the NDSA
accepted.x: The 2025 revision was withdrawn after MoHUA, Metro Rail corporations and the NDSA objected to the cost implications. The 2016 code was restored.
accepted.tq: Match the policy rollback with the specific administrative objection.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which code is currently restored after the withdrawal of the 2025 seismic zoning revision?
accepted.x: The withdrawal of the 2025 revision restored IS 1893 (Part 1): 2016 as the code in force.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the currently restored standard from the withdrawn revision.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the withdrawn 2025 seismic zoning map:
1. It was built by IIT-Madras for the NDMA.
2. It used a probabilistic seismic hazard assessment model.
3. It used 69,519 earthquake events and 36 seismogenic zones.
4. It set peak ground acceleration values from 0.15 g to 0.75 g across Zones II to VI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The withdrawn map was prepared by IIT-Madras for NDMA using PSHA, 69,519 events, 36 seismogenic zones and PGA values of 0.15–0.75 g.
accepted.tq: Check each technical specification separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: Which body is to receive the report of the review panel concerning the withdrawn seismic zoning revision?
accepted.x: The review panel is to submit its report to the Cabinet Secretariat.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority associated with the pending review process.
accepted.sec: Himalaya-Arakan Yoma belt; seismic zones of India

accepted.s: The National Seismological Network of India consists of how many observatories?
accepted.x: The National Seismological Network operated by the National Centre for Seismology consists of 160 observatories.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the network size from the separate GNSS-station figure and event count.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: The National Centre for Seismology detects which combination of earthquakes through its monitoring network?
o: Only earthquakes capable of producing tsunamis
Indian earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above and global earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 and above
Indian earthquakes of magnitude 1.0 and global earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above
Only earthquakes occurring in the Himalayan region
accepted.x: The network detects every Indian earthquake of magnitude 3.0 or above and global earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or above, including tsunami-capable events.
accepted.tq: Separate the two magnitude thresholds instead of treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: The first seismological observatory in India was established at which place in 1898?
accepted.x: India’s first seismological observatory was established at Alipore in Calcutta in 1898.
accepted.tq: Recall the earliest observatory by combining its place and year.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NCS — 34 GNSS stations for crustal strain
GSI — 34 GNSS stations for tracking crustal strain
NCS — first observatory at Alipore in 1898
accepted.x: The Geological Survey of India tracks crustal strain through 34 GNSS stations. The 160-observatory network is operated by the NCS.
accepted.tq: Avoid swapping the monitoring agencies and their respective functions.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: RISEQ, the earthquake-related app of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is now known by which name?
accepted.x: The MoES app RISEQ is now called “Bhookamp.” IndiaQuake is the public-alert app of the National Centre for Seismology.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similarly themed earthquake applications.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: Which application provides public earthquake alerts through the National Centre for Seismology?
o: RISEQ only under its former name
accepted.x: The NCS’s IndiaQuake app provides public earthquake alerts. RISEQ, now called Bhookamp, is the MoES app referred to in the monitoring system.
accepted.tq: Use the app-function distinction rather than relying only on similar names.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India

accepted.s: India developed its Tsunami Early Warning System after which event?
accepted.x: India built its Tsunami Early Warning System after the 2004 Sumatra earthquake and tsunami.
accepted.tq: Match the warning-system initiative with the triggering disaster.
accepted.sec: Seismic monitoring in India
